part_1.description: Personal topics, habits, preferences and familiar experiences

questions: How much walking do you usually do in a day?
Do you prefer walking or taking public transport?
Did you walk more when you were younger?
Where do you usually go for a walk?
Would you like to exercise more in the future?
What kind of food do you usually eat?
Do you often eat food from other countries?
Is there any foreign food that you don't like?
Have you ever tried cooking an international dish?
What Vietnamese food would you recommend to a foreign visitor?
What is your favourite fruit?
How often do you eat fruit?
Is there any fruit you dislike?
Do you prefer fresh fruit or fruit juice?
Is fruit expensive where you live?
Do you often go to cafés?
What do you usually do when you are in a café?
What makes a café attractive to you?
Do you prefer quiet or busy cafés?
Have cafés become more popular among young people?
Do you usually spend holidays with your family or friends?
What kind of holiday do you enjoy most?
What type of accommodation do you prefer?
Do you usually plan your holidays carefully?
Where would you like to go on your next holiday?
Did you enjoy visiting museums when you were a child?
How often do you visit museums nowadays?
Is there an interesting museum near where you live?
Do you prefer visiting museums alone or with other people?
Would you visit a museum when travelling abroad?
What do you think is your best personal quality?
What quality do you value most in a friend?
Are you similar to your parents in terms of personality?
Is there a personal quality you would like to develop?
Do you think you would make a good leader?
How often do you watch films?
What kind of films do you enjoy?
Do you prefer watching films at home or at the cinema?
Is there a film you would like to watch again?
Do you usually watch films alone or with friends?
What kind of music do you usually listen to?
When do you normally listen to music?
Has your taste in music changed over time?
Do you prefer listening to music alone or with other people?
Is live music popular among young people in your country?
How often do you travel by public transport?
Do you enjoy travelling by plane?
What is your favourite way of travelling?
Would you like to live near an airport?
Do you think you will travel more in the future?
What do you usually do at weekends?
Do you prefer relaxing or being active at weekends?
Did you spend your weekends differently when you were younger?
Do you usually make plans for the weekend?
Would you like to have longer weekends?
What do you enjoy most about your studies?
What part of your studies do you find difficult?
Do you prefer studying alone or with other people?
What kind of job would you like to have in the future?
Do you think your studies will help you get that job?
What piece of technology do you use most?
How often do you use your phone?
Is there any technology you find difficult to use?
Did you use technology differently when you were younger?
Is there a new technology you would like to try?
How often do you read or watch the news?
Where do you usually get your news?
Do you prefer local or international news?
Is there a type of news you are particularly interested in?
Do you discuss the news with your friends?
Do you usually make plans for your free time?
Are you good at following your plans?
How often do your plans change?
Do you prefer making plans alone or with other people?
What is one plan you have for the near future?

part_2.description: Cue-card topics requiring a 1–2 minute individual long turn

topics.topic: A Film You Would Like to Watch Again
topics.cue_card: Describe a film you have seen that you would like to watch again.
questions: What the film was and when you watched it
Who you would like to watch it with
Why you would like to watch it again

topics.topic: A Time You Changed a Plan
topics.cue_card: Describe a time when you changed a plan you had made.
questions: What your original plan was
Why you changed it
How you felt about the new plan

topics.topic: A Piece of Work You Were Proud Of
topics.cue_card: Describe a piece of work you did that you felt very satisfied with.
questions: What the work was
Who or what helped you
Why you were satisfied with it

topics.cue_card: Describe a news story that you had a long discussion about.
questions: What the news was about
Who you discussed it with
Why the discussion lasted a long time

topics.cue_card: Describe a law in your country that you think is a good idea.
questions: What the law is
Why and when it was introduced
Why you agree with it

topics.topic: A Person Who Won an Award
topics.cue_card: Describe a person from your country who has won an important award.
questions: Who the person is
What award they received
Why they deserved the award

topics.cue_card: Describe a journey that took longer than you expected.
questions: Where you were going
Who you were travelling with
Why the journey took so long

topics.cue_card: Describe a piece of technology that you find useful.
questions: What it is
How you use it
Why it is useful to you

topics.cue_card: Describe a place you enjoy visiting in your free time.
questions: Where it is
What you do there
Why you enjoy going there

topics.cue_card: Describe someone you know who has a good personal quality.
questions: Who the person is
What quality they have
How this quality has helped them

topics.topic: A Film or Play You Recommend
topics.cue_card: Describe a film or play that you would recommend to a friend.
questions: What it is about
Who you would recommend it to
Why you would recommend it

topics.cue_card: Describe something you achieved that made you feel proud.
questions: What you achieved
How you achieved it
Why it was important to you

topics.topic: A Place You Visited on Holiday
topics.cue_card: Describe a place you visited during a holiday.
questions: Where it was
What you did there
Why you remember the place

topics.cue_card: Describe an interesting conversation you had with someone.
questions: Who you talked to
What you talked about
Why you remember the conversation

topics.topic: Something You Would Like to Learn
topics.cue_card: Describe something new that you would like to learn.
questions: What it is
Why you want to learn it
How you would learn it

part_3.description: Abstract discussion topics involving opinions, causes, comparisons, evaluation and predictions

questions: What kinds of entertainment are most popular among people in your country?
Why do some people prefer watching performances online rather than going to theatres?
What can theatres do to attract younger audiences?
What kinds of rules are necessary in schools?
Why do some students dislike following rules?
How should schools deal with students who repeatedly break rules?
Why do people choose to study law?
What qualities are important for someone working in the legal profession?
Do you think people are more aware of laws than they were in the past?
What factors should young people consider when choosing a career?
How useful is work experience before choosing a career?
Do you think people will change careers more frequently in the future?
What makes people satisfied with their jobs?
Which is more important, a high salary or good colleagues?
Is it possible for people to enjoy every type of job?
Why are some people more ambitious than others?
Is ambition always beneficial?
How do people's ideas of success change as they get older?
How do people usually get news nowadays?
Why do some people prefer local news to international news?
How can people distinguish reliable news from false information?
Why are discussion programmes popular?
What kinds of people are likely to participate in public discussions?
Can public discussions influence people's opinions positively?
How has technology changed people's daily lives?
Do you think people rely too heavily on technology?
What technological developments might change society in the future?
Why do people enjoy watching films?
Do films have an important role in preserving culture?
Will cinemas and theatres remain popular in the future?
Why do many young people want to learn to drive?
What are the main differences between driving in cities and rural areas?
How can governments encourage people to use public transport?
Why are electric cars becoming more popular?
What prevents some people from buying electric cars?
What could governments do to encourage people to use electric vehicles?
Why do people like receiving awards?
Should children receive rewards for good performance at school?
Is competition more beneficial or harmful for young people?
Why do people enjoy travelling to other countries?
What are the benefits of tourism for local communities?
How can countries prevent tourism from damaging local culture and the environment?
Why do people sometimes fail to follow their plans?
Is it better to make detailed plans or remain flexible?
Do you think people today need to adapt to change more than previous generations?
